# backlink-guard
**Check a link source before you submit to it, the link after it goes live, and your own backlinks f
source before you submit to it, the link after it goes live, and your own backlinks for link spam.**
⭐ **37 of 40 Ahrefs-marked spam sites kept from "submit"**, on 100 sites it had never seen · on PyPI
, the official MCP Registry and skills.sh

Find the pages your searchers already land on, the sites that link to your competitors and not to yo
u, the sites Google's AI Overviews cite for your keywords, and what AI assistants answer when asked
for what you make; check a link source **before** you submit your site to it, check the link **after
** it goes live, look at your **own** backlink profile for the patterns Google calls link spam, and
find the links that point at pages of yours that are gone or redirect badly.
Most backlink tools help you send more. This one tells you where not to send, and when to slow down.

## What AI assistants answer: questions and asked
People also ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini directly, and each of them searches the web b
efore it answers. `questions` writes the questions to ask; `asked` puts them to five assistants and
keeps what each one searched for, read and cited.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **questions**: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini each write the questions they expect to be asked (no web

search), merged once: about $0.01.
- **asked**: each question to ChatGPT (its own interface), Googl
e's AI Mode, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini (with their web search). For each assistant, how many ans
wers wrote your domain, gave only your name, cited you, or named a site under your name with another
ending (whose mentions are not counted as yours); then the sites and pages cited most, each with it
s kind and what can honestly be done there, and the searches the assistants ran (AI Mode shows none)

.
- **--rank**: each of those searches on Google and Bing (US, English, top 20). An assistant reads
what its search returns, so a site missing from the results is rarely read at all, and one that rank
s without being cited was passed over. The report says where you rank, and puts the sites on the fir
st page of the most searches next to the answers that cited them.
On 2026-10-26, for agentskillshub.top: 8 questions, 56 answers, 67 searches. No answer read or cited
the site; it was in Google's top 20 for 3 of the 57 searches Google answered and in Bing's for none
of 67. The work is in the search results first.
ChatGPT and Perplexity are asked twice, since their answers vary most: about $0.12 a question with t
he default samples, $0.0035 a search on each engine for `--rank`. `--max-usd` caps the whole run ($1
.00 unless set). Answers asked in the last 7 days come from the cache, so `--rank` after a run costs
nswers asked in the last 7 days come from the cache, so `--rank` after a run costs only the lookups.
## Why
Google's spam updates came in March, June, August and September 2026. "Buying or selling links", "ex
cessive link exchanges", "low-quality directory or bookmark site links" and "using automated program
s or services to create links to your site" are all on Google's list of link spam. Directory lists p
assed around for link building go stale fast and say nothing about any of this.
A verdict here is a set of signals a person can check. It is not Google's judgment: nobody outside G
oogle can tell whether one link is counted, ignored or held against a site. Google ignores most junk
links. What the tool is good for is not wasting effort on dead, empty or link-selling sites, and no
t building the pattern yourself.
